title: Bump GitHub Actions to Node.js 24-compatible versions
description: GitHub will force Node.js 24 by default on 02-06-2026 and remove Node.js 20 from runners on 16-09-2026. The CI annotation observed on run 25124977134 (29-04-2026) flagged actions/checkout@v4 as still running on Node.js 20. Audit .github/workflows/ for any actions still pinned to Node-20 versions (checkout, rust-cache, etc.), bump to current major versions that publish Node-24 builds. Re-run a CI job and confirm the deprecation annotation is gone. No code change expected outside .github/workflows/.

title: Add 'connections withdraw <invitation_urn>' (RE capture required)
description: Every invite the CLI sends is now an outstanding Pending; users have no way to undo via CLI. The withdraw flow likely lives on the same MemberRelationships resource under a different action. Capture the live web withdraw flow (Pending → click → confirm), document body shape in re/connection_request.md, then add the command. Uses the same retry middleware once it lands.
notes: Investigation 2026-04-29: re/invitations.md already documents the WITHDRAW action in InvitationActionsRepository. Sibling action 'accept' is implemented at linkedin/linkedin-api/src/client.rs:1902 (path: voyagerRelationshipsDashInvitations/{urn}?action=accept, body: {invitationUrn, sharedSecret}). Withdraw likely parallels — replace 'accept' with 'withdraw' in path. BUT: no get_sent_invitations() exists yet (only get_invitations() for received), so users can't easily obtain the URN. Bead's 'RE capture required' tag still stands — need to verify (a) WITHDRAW body shape matches, (b) sent-invitation URN format, (c) whether sent invitations have sharedSecret field. Captured live web flow would resolve all three.

title: Add custom-invite/preload page as fallback slug→URN resolver
description: When the GraphQL profile resolver returns transient downstream errors, hitting linkedin.com/preload/custom-invite/?vanityName=<slug> returns the resolved URN in the response (the modern web client uses this as a server-side resolver). Add it as a fallback after the GraphQL retry middleware exhausts its retries. More reliable than retry-and-pray when the GraphQL path is genuinely down.
notes: Added resolve_profile_urn_via_preload as a final fallback after the existing 3-step REST/GraphQL chain. Pulls /preload/custom-invite/?vanityName=<slug>, finds the publicIdentifier:<slug> marker in the embedded HTML-escaped JSON state, walks back ~500 bytes to grab the paired entityUrn. Disambiguates correctly from the viewer's own URN that also appears earlier in the page (me-menu/global nav). 4 unit tests including the disambiguation case and an out-of-window negative.

title: Expose mentions in 'notifications list' / add 'notifications mentions N'
description: Notifications carry an underlying post URN; the post body has structured mention data with fsd_profile URNs. Surface that list either inline (--with-mentions flag on list) or as a separate subcommand 'notifications mentions N' indexing into last list. Closes the workflow gap where users have to chase the post URL to enumerate who else was tagged.
notes: Investigation 2026-04-29: cmd_notifications_list at linkedin/linkedin-cli/src/main.rs:4842, get_notifications at client.rs:961. print_notification_card already extracts contentPrimaryText[0].text but treats it as flat string. No notifications cache exists — would need to add last_notifications.json paralleling feed_cache_path() at main.rs:5317. NO documentation in re/ for the structured mention shape (attributesV2 entries with MEMBER_MENTION type + fsd_profile URN). The post body fetch via permalink endpoint is also undocumented (overlaps with linkedin-rs-0hw). Two captures needed: (1) a notification card with mention metadata to confirm whether attributesV2 lives on contentPrimaryText[0] or fetched separately, (2) the permalink endpoint to fetch the underlying post body. Suggest implementing 0hw first since oau depends on its endpoint.

title: Add '--summary' flag to 'profile view' for compact output
description: Default --json dumps ~150KB per profile including positions, education, certifications, ring status, etc. Add --summary that returns only: full URN, public ID, name, headline, location, relationship state (connection/noConnection/etc), follower count. Plays well with batch flows and avoids hitting the output-size guard.
notes: Added --summary flag to profile view that returns compact JSON: name, public ID, full URN, headline, location, industry, relationshipState (the union key inside memberRelationship.memberRelationship), followerCount. New extract_profile_summary helper with 3 unit tests. Conflicts with --json (clap-enforced). Follower count is sourced from profileProfileActions.overflowActionsResolutionResults[].followingState.followerCount.

title: Classify CLI errors with actionable next-step hints
description: Today errors like 'API error (HTTP 301): {"status":301}' or 'failed to resolve profile' offer no diagnostic signal. Add a thin classifier that distinguishes: auth-stale (suggest 'li auth login'), endpoint-retired (suggest checking re/ docs and filing an issue), rate-limited (suggest backoff), transient (already retried by the new middleware). Output the hint as a second line on stderr.
notes: Added error_hint(msg) returning Some(&'static str) when an error matches a known shape: HTTP 401 (suggests li auth login), HTTP 301 (endpoint retired — check re/ docs), HTTP 429 (rate limited), GraphQL transient (retried already), failed to resolve profile (suggest URN or search invite N), HTTP 403 (captcha), index out of range (rerun parent command). 6 unit tests. Hint prints as a second line on stderr after the error message; exit code is unchanged.

title: Make 'feed view <urn>' fall back to the post permalink endpoint
description: Currently 'feed view' only works if the post is in the last 50 scanned feed items, returning a 404 otherwise. Add a fallback path that fetches the post via LinkedIn's permalink endpoint (the same one /feed/update/<urn> hits in the web UI) so any activity URN works. Keep the cache-hit fast path.
notes: Investigation 2026-04-29: get_post() at linkedin/linkedin-api/src/client.rs:516 currently fetches feed/updates?q=findFeed&start=0&count=50 and scans for activity ID match. cmd_feed_view at linkedin/linkedin-cli/src/main.rs:5597 calls it directly. Permalink endpoint NOT documented in re/. api_endpoint_catalog.md shows feed/updates/{updateId}?action=feedback (POST actions only) — GET-by-URN permalink path/params unknown. Need to capture web flow: visit linkedin.com/feed/update/urn:li:activity:N in browser devtools, log the voyager API call. Likely candidates to verify: feed/updates/{urlEncodedUrn}, feed/feedDashUpdatesV2/{urn}, or a Dash GraphQL finder. Once endpoint known, fallback should: 1) try cache scan (current 50-item path), 2) on miss, hit permalink endpoint, 3) only error if both miss.

title: Add 'search invite N' that uses last search-people result by index
description: Mirror the 'feed read N' / 'feed comments N' pattern: after a search people query, allow inviting the Nth result by its row index in the printed list. Removes the URN-extraction friction users hit when piping search results into invite. Reuse the existing search cache file.
notes: Added 'search invite <index>' subcommand. Pulls fsd_profile URN out of cached entityResult (preferred path — bypasses GraphQL profile resolver entirely) and falls back to slug if entityUrn/trackingUrn are absent. New SearchPersonTarget struct + resolve_search_person_target helper. 3 unit tests cover URN-preferred, slug-fallback, and label formatting.

title: Add 'connections invite-batch' for newline-separated URNs/slugs
description: Replace the bash-loop pattern users currently rely on. Read URNs/slugs from --from-file or stdin, send each through send_connection_request with built-in 2s pacing and per-line success/failure reporting. Should depend on the new retry middleware so transient failures don't break a 50-item batch.
notes: Added 'connections invite-batch --from-file <path|->' that reads slugs/URNs (one per line, # comments and blanks ignored) and sends each with pacing_ms delay (default 2s). Tab-separated stdout: <input>\tOK\t<invitation_urn> or <input>\tFAIL\t<reason>. Continues through failures unless --stop-on-error is set; closes with a summary line on stderr. Uses the new GraphQL retry middleware so transient downstream errors don't break a 50-line batch. 2 unit tests on the parser (parse_batch_targets).

title: Retry transient GraphQL 'Internal error fetching data from downstream' errors
description: LinkedIn's GraphQL mesh returns transient downstream errors at HTTP 200 with a body that mixes partial data and error strings. Today the client treats them as terminal, leaking out as hard CLI errors. Add bounded exponential backoff (max 2 retries; 500ms then 1500ms) inside the post/get layer for this specific error class. Don't retry on auth errors or 4xx-equivalent shapes. Test with a fault-injecting fake transport.
notes: Wrapped graphql_get and graphql_post in retry loops keyed off is_retriable_graphql_error, which matches HTTP-200 GraphQL bodies containing 'Internal error fetching data from downstream' or 'Failed to get response from server'. Reuses existing MAX_RETRIES / BASE_BACKOFF_MS / MAX_BACKOFF_MS constants. 6 new unit tests.

title: Migrate send_connection_request from retired normInvitations to Dash endpoint
description: LinkedIn retired the legacy voyagerGrowthNormInvitations endpoint. As of 29-04-2026 every POST returns HTTP 301. Fix: switch to voyagerRelationshipsDashInvitations?action=create. Body schema captured from live web UI since the Dash schema in the RE doc was incomplete.
notes: Captured the modern endpoint from a live web Connect flow. The replacement is voyagerRelationshipsDashMemberRelationships?action=verifyQuotaAndCreateV2&decorationId=...InvitationCreationResultWithInvitee-2 — neither the legacy normInvitations nor the Dash Invitations route the RE doc anticipated. Body is just {invitee:{inviteeUnion:{memberProfile:<full-urn>}}}; no trackingId. Smoke-tested on one URN with the new code; LinkedIn returned a fresh fsd_invitation URN. Follow-ups (out of scope): with-note message placement is unverified, email invitee variant unmapped, withdraw flow likely also moved to MemberRelationships.

title: events attendees returns empty on stale session
description: First call to li events attendees returned empty elements array. Same call worked after Chrome browsed LinkedIn (likely refreshed shared cookies). Investigate: should CLI detect stale sessions and prompt re-auth? Should it warn instead of silently returning empty?
close_reason: Already resolved by 2a0bad8 (Add events commands: view details and list attendees). cmd_event_attendees in linkedin/linkedin-cli/src/main.rs:6052-6062 detects the empty-on-stale-session case via a get_event probe and prints a warning to stderr telling the user to refresh cookies and re-run `li auth login`. Bead never got closed when the fix landed; cleaning up retroactively.
